named.role: Primary answer-span routing candidate: A strongly selects proposed answers through a copy-capable OV map, whereas B usually selects question information. Recency-sensitive rather than a reliable belief tracker.
Source- and template-sensitive answer retrieval candidate. A shows stronger user-answer preference under matched-speaker controls, with identity-preserving weight geometry.
Question-versus-proposed-answer routing candidate: A shifts toward the proposed answer while B emphasizes question information; OV geometry supports identity transfer.

Strong identity-preserving channel and candidate answer-context binder. A more strongly attends to belief/answer markers at guessed-answer positions and often retrieves the guess at response positions.

Distributed numerical readout candidate: 42.9% of its down-projection difference lies in the nine-dimensional digit-contrast subspace. Actual unit activation and causal behavioral contribution remain unknown.
Additional answer-content retrieval candidate in A. Copy interpretation is stronger for letters and cities; digit geometry depends on inclusion of learned normalization diagonals.
Distributed numerical readout and competition candidate: 27.8% of down-projection difference lies in digit-contrast directions; includes identifiable zero- and four-associated weight features.
Candidate answer-context binding pathway: A's guessed-answer positions attend substantially more to nearby belief/answer markers; its OV map is identity-preserving.
Earlier numerical readout candidate: 14.9% of down-projection difference lies in digit-contrast directions, approximately nine times the random-token-subspace baseline.
Counterbalancing candidate with identity-suppressing OV geometry and increased guess attention in A. Its net effect on sycophancy is not established.
Strongest observed source selector: B redirects an identity-preserving transport map from question content toward the user's proposed answer; causal control may be upstream.
Reads task relations and arithmetic operators in A; is strongly diverted toward guess-related context in B.
Transports operands and question content; A retains task access while B substantially reduces it when guesses are present.
Entity and lexical-content transport candidate, with strong positive lexical OV alignment and question-to-guess routing shifts in B.
Parallel identity-preserving task-content transport branch that shifts toward proposed answers in B.
Additional identity-preserving lexical-content branch, with reduced task-content access in B on factual guess prompts.
Auxiliary identity-preserving content transport; favors task content more in A and proposed answers more in B.

Distributed late numeric and label readout candidate; output-column changes selectively affect numeric contrasts and strengthen B's algebraic identity alignment, without established activation-level effects.
Distributed preceding numeric and label readout candidate, supported by answer-contrast projections and two separate input/output weight-alignment diagnostics.
User-guess-selective reader in B, including when another person's guess occurs later; transport signs depend on the answer family.

Strongest candidate for stated-choice-to-option-content retrieval. B tracks the stated choice independently of correctness; OV products robustly preserve tested answer distinctions. Local causal attribution remains unverified.
Candidate stated-answer or label retriever and query preparer for L11H2. B retrieves the stated label more strongly; local query-side changes increase a static number-category association.
Candidate downstream guessed-content retrieval, particularly for factual word answers. Strong choice tracking in B and positive word-pair OV contrasts; numeric interpretation is less robust.
Candidate upstream label/content transport into the choice-selection route. Increased stated-label attention in B and robust positive static copying contrasts.
Candidate label-to-content binding and stated-label retrieval bridge. Supported by attention and compositional weight products, but some output signs depend on scaling.
Additional candidate stated-label retrieval route in B, contrasting with more question-directed attention in A on initial probes.

Late answer-content matching and possible suppression or feedback. Attention often tracks truth in A and the stated choice in B; positive same-token QK matching accompanies frequently negative word-output contrasts.
Candidate numeric-representation conditioning before L11H2. Changed ungated read/write products have number-sensitive input directions; actual gated and causal effects are unresolved.
Candidate numeric-content transformation following retrieval. Number-sensitive read/write differences are evident, with a substantial down-projection contribution in static decomposition.
Candidate late numeric-answer reweighting. Distributed changes affect numeral-distinguishing write directions; no individual unit or behavioural effect is established.
